en: The Banaue Rice Terraces in the Philippines use the inclined plane simple machine to help farmers carry crops up steep mountains.
Teflon is a synthetic material applied to frying pans to significantly reduce friction and prevent food from sticking.
Sir Isaac Newton formulated the law of universal gravitation to explain why objects fall toward the Earth.
Ancient navigators used naturally magnetized pieces of the mineral lodestone to create the very first magnetic compasses.
Italian physicist Alessandro Volta invented the voltaic pile, which was the world's first electrical battery.
Fireflies produce visible light through a chemical reaction inside their abdomens called bioluminescence to attract mates.
Bottlenose dolphins use high-frequency sound waves in a process called echolocation to navigate and hunt underwater.
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay harnesses underground heat energy from volcanoes to generate electricity.
Roller coasters at Enchanted Kingdom convert gravitational potential energy into kinetic energy as they drop down steep hills.
The metal blade of an axe acts as a wedge to split firewood by concentrating force into a narrow area.
Junkyards use giant electromagnets powered by electric currents to lift and move heavy scrap metal cars.
The construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza involved using simple pulley systems to lift massive limestone blocks.
